speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) whether the Ministry will review the entry criteria for dental surgery assistants who are keen to switch to a nursing career but do not meet the minimum Grade Point Average requirement; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider a bridging programme for such dental surgery assistants so that they can pursue a diploma in nursing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am encouraged by the drive of Dental Surgery Assistants (DSAs) to want to upgrade themselves, including switching to a nursing career.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: From an interest and aptitude point of view, an enthused DSA is more likely to be committed to a nursing or healthcare-related career.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are a few realistic pathways for a DSA to take on a nursing career.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They may also apply for admission into the ITE Skills Certificate programmes in healthcare to become Healthcare or Clinic Assistants.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Such open accessibility is a key principle of adult training and lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, as Ms Thanaletchmi has raised, it is an important and broader question about lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I just wish to clarify the point on whether some of the programmes for upgrading, especially in the health profession, can be made modular.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Because there are people who find it difficult to go on full-time study with so many other commitments, although they are under the Professional Conversion Programme, and whether modular aspects of a training programme, some form of bridging can be considered.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are several key principles of lifelong learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Like what I mentioned earlier, open accessibility is one.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for nursing, it is something that we will have to study as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as the Member know, in nursing training, there is also a lot of dedication and some full-time dedication is also required especially when you are on attachment to a hospital.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But within the limits of professional requirements, we will certainly go in that direction.
